questions: Are you currently experiencing any change in vision?
Do you have pain when moving either eye?
Have you noticed a sudden change in the appearance or position of either eye?
Have you noticed that one eye does not move normally?
Have you noticed drooping, retraction, or difficulty closing either eyelid?
Have you had redness, discharge, swelling, or marked sensitivity to light?
Have you experienced flashes of light, new floaters, or a curtain-like shadow in your vision?
Did these eye changes begin suddenly?
Have you recently injured your head or either eye?
Have you ever had eye surgery or a significant eye condition?
Have you had headaches, weakness, numbness, difficulty speaking, or trouble walking?
Have you had symptoms of an overactive thyroid, such as unexplained weight loss, heat intolerance, tremor, palpitations, or increased sweating?
Have you ever been diagnosed with thyroid disease?
Have you had recent fever or a significant infection?
Are you taking any new medicines or recreational drugs?

results: 1. Monocular and binocular visual acuity testing
not performed / not available
2. Formal ocular alignment and motility examination in the nine diagnostic positions of gaze
nystagmus: direction and whether it changes with gaze: no nystagmus
adduction in horizontal gaze (each eye): on left gaze the right eye fails to adduct, and the contralateral eye shows NO abducting nystagmus - unlike a classic INO
abducting nystagmus of the fellow eye: absent
vertical gaze and convergence: mild vertical limitation and mildly impaired convergence
3. Alternate-cover and prism-cover testing at distance and near
skew deviation / alternating cover test: no vertical misalignment
4. Examination for ptosis, eyelid retraction, fatigability, and orbicularis oculi weakness
ptosis / lid position: partial ptosis
5. Pupillary examination in bright and dim illumination, including assessment for a relative afferent pupillary defect
pupil size and light reaction: pupils EQUALLY REACTIVE - pupil-sparing
6. Saccadic and smooth-pursuit eye-movement testing
smooth pursuit and saccades: normal
7. Sustained upgaze testing for fatigability
not performed / not available
8. Ice-pack test over the more symptomatic eyelid
not performed / not available
9. ACh receptor antibody testing, including binding, blocking, and modulating antibodies
anti-acetylcholine receptor antibodies: negative
10. MuSK antibody testing
acetylcholine receptor, MuSK and LRP4 antibodies: normal
11. Thyroid-stimulating hormone, free T4, and free T3 testing
TSH / free T4: normal
12. MRI of the brain and orbits with and without gadolinium contrast
MRI brain with gadolinium: small dorsal paramedian midbrain infarct
MRI sella and orbits: normal pituitary and orbits
13. Magnetic resonance angiography of the intracranial circulation
CT / MR angiography (circle of Willis): no aneurysm
14. Single-fiber electromyography of an extraocular or facial muscle
single-fibre electromyography: normal
